LLMOps

Managing Large Language Models
in Production

LLMOps：生产环境中的大语言模型管理

Abi Aryan

— 原书第 2 页 —

“Developing with AI is getting easier, but production is where the real challenges lie. This book is the essential guide I'll use to teach my students how to navigate the complexities of LLMOps and successfully deploy large language models in the real world. With clarity and actionable solutions, LLMOps is a vital read for transforming LLM prototypes into robust, production-ready AI systems.”

“用 AI 开发正变得越来越容易，但生产环境才是真正挑战所在。这本书正是我会用来教学生的必备指南——带他们穿越 LLMOps 的复杂性，在真实世界成功部署大语言模型。凭借清晰的讲解和可落地的方案，《LLMOps》是把 LLM 原型转化为健壮、可投产 AI 系统的必读之作。”

Ammar Mohanna, lead AI consultant at EDT&Partners and lecturer at the American University of Beirut

——Ammar Mohanna，EDT&Partners 首席 AI 顾问，贝鲁特美国大学讲师

“This book demystifies LLMOps with clear, actionable guidance—a perfect resource for ML engineers, platform teams, and anyone taking LLMs from prototype to production.”

“这本书以清晰、可落地的指引揭开 LLMOps 的神秘面纱——是 ML 工程师、平台团队以及任何把 LLM 从原型推向生产的人的完美资源。”

Nirmal Budhathoki, senior data scientist, Microsoft

——Nirmal Budhathoki，微软资深数据科学家

Here's the thing about large language models: they don't play by the old rules. Traditional MLOps completely falls apart when you're dealing with GenAI. The model hallucinates, security assumptions crumble, monitoring breaks, and agents can't operate. Suddenly you're in uncharted territory. That's exactly why LLMOps has emerged as its own discipline.

关于大语言模型，事情是这样的：它们不按老规矩出牌。当你面对生成式 AI 时，传统 MLOps 完全失效。模型会幻觉，安全假设崩塌，监控失灵，智能体无法运作。你突然置身于未知领地。这正是 LLMOps 作为一门独立学科崛起的原因。

LLMOps: Managing Large Language Models in Production is your guide to actually running these systems when real users and real money are on the line. This book isn't about building cool demos. It's about keeping LLM systems running smoothly in the real world.

《LLMOps：生产环境中的大语言模型管理》是你在真实用户和真金白银押注时真正运维这些系统的指南。这本书不是教你做酷炫 demo，而是教你在真实世界让 LLM 系统平稳运行。

  • Navigate the new roles and processes that LLM operations require理清 LLM 运维所需的新角色与新流程
  • Monitor LLM performance when traditional metrics don't tell the whole story在传统指标无法说明全貌时监控 LLM 性能
  • Set up evaluations, governance, and security audits that actually matter for GenAI建立对生成式 AI 真正重要的评估、治理和安全审计
  • Wrangle the operational mess of agents, RAG systems, and evolving prompts搞定智能体、RAG 系统和不断演进的提示所带来的运维乱局
  • Scale infrastructure without burning through your compute budget在不烧光算力预算的前提下扩缩基础设施

Abi Aryan is the founder of Abide AI and a machine learning research engineer with nearly a decade of experience building production-level ML systems. A mathematician by training, she previously served as a visiting research scholar at the Cognitive Systems Lab at UCLA, under Dr. Judea Pearl, where she focused on developing intelligent agents. She's currently advancing research in reflective intelligence in AI agents, distributed self-healing protocols for multi-agent systems, and GPU engineering for very-large-scale AI systems.

Abi Aryan 是 Abide AI 的创始人，也是一名机器学习研究工程师，拥有近十年构建生产级 ML 系统的经验。她是数学科班出身，曾作为访问研究学者在 UCLA 认知系统实验室跟随 Judea Pearl 博士工作，专注于开发智能体。她目前的研究方向包括 AI 智能体中的反思智能、多智能体系统的分布式自愈协议，以及超大规模 AI 系统的 GPU 工程。

— 原书第 6 页 —

Chapter 1 introduces LLMs: key terms, transformer models, architectures (encoder-only, decoder-only, encoder–decoder, state-space, small language models), how to choose an LLM, open source versus proprietary, enterprise use cases, and ten challenges of building with LLMs.

第 1 章介绍 LLM：关键术语、Transformer 模型、架构（仅编码器、仅解码器、编码器–解码器、状态空间、小语言模型）、如何选择 LLM、开源与专有之争、企业用例，以及构建 LLM 应用的十大挑战。

Chapter 2 introduces LLMOps: operational frameworks, the shift from MLOps to LLMOps, LLMOps teams and roles, the four goals (reliability, scalability, robustness, security), and the LLMOps maturity model.

第 2 章介绍 LLMOps：运维框架、从 MLOps 到 LLMOps 的转变、LLMOps 团队与角色、四大目标（可靠性、可扩展性、鲁棒性、安全）以及 LLMOps 成熟度模型。

Chapter 3 covers LLM-based applications: using AI models in applications, infrastructure applications such as agentic workflows, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, the rise of vLLMs and multimodal LLMs, and how to control and monitor them.

第 3 章讨论基于 LLM 的应用：在应用中使用 AI 模型、基础设施应用（如 agentic 工作流）、模型上下文协议（MCP）、智能体间协议（A2A）、vLLM 与多模态 LLM 的兴起，以及如何控制和监控它们。

— 原书第 7 页 —

Chapter 4 covers data engineering for LLMs: the DataOps engineer role, data management, synthetic data, LLM pipelines, training an LLM, data composition, scaling laws, data repetition and quality, a general 10-step data-preprocessing pipeline, and vectorization with vector databases.

第 4 章讨论 LLM 的数据工程：DataOps 工程师角色、数据管理、合成数据、LLM 流水线、训练 LLM、数据构成、缩放定律、数据重复与质量、通用的 10 步数据预处理流水线，以及向量库与向量化。

Chapter 5 covers model domain adaptation: training LLMs from scratch, model ensembling, prompt engineering (one/few-shot, chain-of-thought, RAG, Semantic Kernel), fine-tuning (adapters, prefix tuning, PEFT, instruction tuning, RLHF), mixture of experts, and model optimization for resource-constrained devices.

第 5 章讨论模型领域适配：从头训练 LLM、模型集成、提示工程（单样本/少样本、思维链、RAG、Semantic Kernel）、微调（适配器、前缀调优、PEFT、指令微调、RLHF）、混合专家，以及面向资源受限设备的模型优化。

— 原书第 8 页 —

Chapter 6 covers API-first LLM deployment: deploying your model, containerization, pipeline automation, workflow orchestration, monitoring, developing REST APIs, credential management, API gateways and versioning, deployment architectures (modular/monolithic/microservices), automating RAG and knowledge graph updates, latency optimization, and orchestrating multiple models.

第 6 章讨论 API 优先的 LLM 部署：部署模型、容器化、流水线自动化、工作流编排、监控、开发 REST API、凭据管理、API 网关与版本管理、部署架构（模块化/单体/微服务）、自动化 RAG 与知识图更新、延迟优化，以及多模型编排。

Chapter 7 covers evaluation for LLMs: why evaluation is hard, evaluating performance, metrics for RAG and agentic systems, general evaluation considerations, traditional metrics' limits, and the observability pipeline.

第 7 章讨论 LLM 评估：评估为何是难题、性能评估、RAG 与 agentic 系统的指标、通用评估考量、传统指标的局限，以及可观测性流水线。

— 原书第 9 页 —

Chapter 8 covers governance: monitoring, privacy, and security—the data issue, security risks (prompt injection, jailbreaking, other risks), defensive measures via LLMSecOps, and a 10-step LLMSecOps audit.

第 8 章讨论治理：监控、隐私与安全——数据问题、安全风险（提示注入、越狱、其他风险）、通过 LLMSecOps 采取的防御措施，以及 10 步 LLMSecOps 审计。

Chapter 9 covers scaling: hardware, infrastructure, and resource management—choosing an approach, monitoring, A/B and shadow testing, automatic infrastructure provisioning, the compute-optimal argument, optimizing infrastructure (kernel fusion, precision scaling, parallel/distributed computing), ZeRO/DeepSpeed, and backup/failsafe processes.

第 9 章讨论扩缩：硬件、基础设施与资源管理——选择方式、监控、A/B 与影子测试、基础设施自动供给、算力最优论证、优化基础设施（内核融合、精度缩放、并行/分布式计算）、ZeRO/DeepSpeed，以及备份与故障保障流程。

— 原书第 10 页 —

Chapter 10 looks forward to the future of LLMs and LLMOps: scaling beyond current boundaries, hybrid neurosymbolic architectures, sparse and mixture-of-experts models, memory-augmented models, interpretable and self-optimizing models, cross-model collaboration, RAG's future, advances in GPU technology, data management, privacy and security, evaluation frameworks, and how to succeed as an LLMOps engineer.

第 10 章展望 LLM 与 LLMOps 的未来：超越当前边界的扩缩、神经符号混合架构、稀疏与混合专家模型、记忆增强模型、可解释与自优化模型、跨模型协作、RAG 的未来、GPU 技术进步、数据管理、隐私与安全、评估框架，以及如何成为成功的 LLMOps 工程师。

The book closes with an Index, About the Author, and a Colophon.

全书以索引、作者简介和版权页结束。

Preface前言

I've lost count of how many times I've been asked, “What's the difference between an LLM/AI engineer and an LLMOps engineer?” It's one of those questions that keep popping up, whether I'm in a meeting, at a conference, or just grabbing coffee with someone in the field.

我已经记不清被问过多少次：“LLM/AI 工程师和 LLMOps 工程师有什么区别？”这个问题总是反复出现——无论我是在开会、在会议上，还是和同行一起喝咖啡。

I used to start by explaining the technical distinctions between the roles. But over time, I realized the real issue: people don't fully grasp what it takes to keep the lights on with large language models (LLMs) in production over an extended period.

我过去会先解释这两个角色的技术区别。但久而久之，我意识到真正的问题在于：人们并未充分理解，要在生产环境中长期让大语言模型（LLM）“灯火通明”地运转，究竟需要付出什么。

As I write this in early 2025, the top models, techniques, and best practices are changing every few days. Thus, very few people understand their complexity. Most people still think of operationalizing, or “Ops,” as deployment, but in the LLM context, Ops is really about streamlining people, processes, and technology to make these models secure, robust, and reliable in production.

在 2025 年初写作本书时，顶尖模型、技术和最佳实践每隔几天就变一次。因此很少有人理解其复杂性。多数人仍把“运维化”（即“Ops”）等同于部署，但在 LLM 语境下，Ops 真正关乎的是理顺人、流程和技术，让这些模型在生产中安全、鲁棒、可靠。

Enterprises and their human resource departments are scrambling to figure out what it all means for their teams and their projects, and in this book I have done my best to answer that question. This book isn't a tutorial on defining roles or how to build and deploy an LLM; while it touches on both of those topics, that isn't enough anymore. Once LLM-based applications are in production, someone has to keep them optimized, or they risk becoming overengineered solutions to simple problems or, worse, badly maintained houses of cards that crumble under high demand or a prompt injection attack.

企业及其人力资源部门正忙于搞清楚这一切对他们的团队和项目意味着什么，本书中我尽我所能回答了这个问题。本书不是一本定义角色或如何构建、部署 LLM 的教程；虽然它都有所涉及，但这些已经不够了。基于 LLM 的应用一旦投产，就必须有人持续让它们保持优化，否则它们可能沦为对简单问题的过度工程化方案，甚至更糟——变成维护不善的纸牌屋，在高负载或一次提示注入攻击下轰然倒塌。

In traditional software development (or Software 2.0), you wouldn't ask your lead developer to build and maintain your entire product. Software development engineers build, and reliability engineers maintain. Building and maintaining LLMs requires a similar separation of duties. In Software 3.0, LLM/AI engineers build and LLMOps engineers maintain!

在传统软件开发（或软件 2.0）中，你不会让首席开发既构建又维护整个产品。软件开发工程师负责构建，可靠性工程师负责维护。构建和运维 LLM 也需要类似的职责分离。在软件 3.0 中，LLM/AI 工程师负责构建，LLMOps 工程师负责运维！

— 原书第 14 页 —

Although machine learning operations (MLOps) are foundational to LLMOps, the MLOps skills that engineers gain from working on structured data and discriminative models don't fully translate to generative models.

尽管机器学习运维（MLOps）是 LLMOps 的基础，但工程师在结构化数据和判别式模型上获得的 MLOps 技能，并不能完全迁移到生成式模型上。

In short, I'm writing this book to help you appreciate the unique aspects of the full LLM-based application lifecycle, from data engineering to model deployment and API design to monitoring, security, and resource optimization. I want to give you a strong foundation for making decisions as you build, maintain, and optimize your LLM data, models, and applications.

简而言之，我写这本书是为了帮助你领会整个基于 LLM 应用生命周期的独特之处——从数据工程到模型部署和 API 设计，再到监控、安全和资源优化。我想为你打下坚实基础，让你在构建、运维和优化 LLM 数据、模型与应用时做出决策。

Conventions Used in This Book本书使用的约定

The following typographical conventions are used in this book: Italic indicates new terms, URLs, email addresses, filenames, and file extensions. Constant width is used for program listings, as well as within paragraphs to refer to program elements such as variable or function names, databases, data types, environment variables, statements, and keywords.

本书使用以下排版约定：斜体用于新术语、URL、邮箱地址、文件名和文件扩展名。等宽字体用于程序清单，以及在段落中指代变量或函数名、数据库、数据类型、环境变量、语句和关键字等程序元素。
